Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader), part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How does a writer make a story interesting? 2. Which qualities of a person can animals be given?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively to dramatise selected parts of the story.

Values:
Responsibility is promoted as the learner takes up tasks assigned to them as they dramatise the story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Decision Making is enhanced as the learner identifies instances of personification and flashback.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: How does a writer make a story interesting? 2. Which qualities of a person can animals be given?
